newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle close weak.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle close weak.

text.p: An expected easier tone in cash fed cattle markets as prices appered to have topped pressured CME live and feeder cattle futures, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.625 to 0.300 cent per lb lower with August off most at 64.075 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.425 lower to 0.150 higher with August off 0.425 at 78.200 cents.

Packers showed reduced interest for fed cattle during the day and pulled back on their bids and this prompted selling interest in live cattle futures. Ideas of $65 per cwt sales in the panhandle gave way to talk that $64 will now be the high for the recent price rise, traders said.

Packers pulled back as sales of boxed beef slowed and seasonal considerations started to weigh on sentiment. Beef prices will top soon when retailers finish last minute purchases for the July 4th holiday and beef prices decline seasonally during the remainder of the summer. Heavy feedlot supplies will also weigh on fed cattle prices the next couple of months, they said.
RBH continued to pressure August with Cargill Investor Services a late seller. In live cattle options, commission houses sold August 66 calls and October 69 and 70 calls, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle also came under pressure despite lower corn futures. Any retreat in fed cattle prices will make feeder cattle prices look even more out of line, traders said.
"Fundamentally, feeders are overpriced," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc.
Clarkson noted that even with grains lower traders can not continue to buy feeders at current price levels and make money. There is no hedge against the October live cattle contract, he added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.14 at $77.60 per cwt.
General local selling offset mixed active fund buying late. Locals sold nearbys and bought deferred live cattle against the sales in feeders, pit sources said.
Boneless beef and boneless beef trimming futures retreated for losses in most months by the close after showing early gains in their third full day of trade, traders said.

Early strength in cash boneless beef supported that market early but seasonals turned the market lower. Cash boneless should remain strong into the July 4th holiday and then will turn lower seasonally before firming again before the Labor Day holiday. Bear spreading by Lind-Waldock added to pressure in nearbys, they said.
Trimmings followed the lead of live cattle futures and eased to a new contract low in August on expectaions prices will decline soon and supplies will be adequate, they said.
Boneless beef closed 0.80 cent per lb lower to 1.70 higher with August off most at 94.20 cents. Trimmings ended 1.40 lower to unchanged with August off most had 42.50 cents.
